candidates.title: Summarize resume email threads

demandEvidence.chore: Reference an original resume email by immutable ID and prepare a compact summary with a draft prefill.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: To save email resume properly, i need immutable id to reference original email of the resume.

experimentPlan.output: A compact resume-email summary tied to a supplied stable message reference.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator pastes one fictional thread and its reference ID.
steps: Check that the supplied reference is present.
Extract the stated role, request and response status into labeled fields.
Draft a short summary linked to the supplied reference.
Flag missing or conflicting facts for review.
Compare the output with a manually prepared answer key.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a fixed synthetic set, verify every output field against the answer key and confirm the reference is copied exactly.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies sanitized test text and fields, verifies the summary and reference, and authorizes any use with real email.
unverified: Whether any email system exposes a stable immutable ID to a prototype
Whether summaries preserve context accurately across long threads
Any email connector or automated drafting capability

ease.reason: A student can test operator-supplied sample email text, but no implementation reference supports email access or immutable IDs.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: recruiting or professional-service operators might pay for faster email review; this request proves no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare a supplied thread and reference ID with a summary, but email integration and identity stability are unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed text-to-summary loop is bounded; a person must verify identity, context and every prefilled detail, and no automation support is documented.

evidence.reason: The native context describes resume email summarization and immutable-ID need, but gives no repeated volume or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore merits a bounded proposed experiment, but no supplied implementation reference supports the mechanics; conservative provisional mean is below 6.

candidates.title: Draft booking and service status alerts

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare booking confirmations, provider assignment notifications, payment status updates and customer alerts.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How can n8n help automate booking confirmations, provider assignment notifications, payment status updates, and customer alerts?

experimentPlan.output: A review queue of proposed status messages for a small set of fictional bookings.
experimentPlan.trigger: A labeled synthetic booking event is added to a test sheet.
steps: Validate required test fields and flag missing values.
Select a draft template for the declared event type.
Fill only fields supplied in the test record.
Mark duplicate event IDs and simulated failures.
Show the draft and flags in a review queue.
Compare each draft and flag with expected test outputs.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For fixed synthetic events, check correct template, exact field values, duplicate detection and failure flags against a written answer key.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator defines allowed statuses and templates, verifies payment facts, and approves every customer or provider message.
unverified: Whether booking or payment APIs can be accessed
Whether event IDs support reliable deduplication and retries
Any integration, delivery or persistence capability

ease.reason: The request names four alert types, but no supplied implementation reference documents integrations or message delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: on-demand service operators might pay for fewer missed updates; the discussion establishes need, not purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic event-to-draft prototype can cover labeled booking states; APIs, payment correctness and production delivery remain unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A proposed event-to-draft loop can repeat, but no automation capability is evidenced and a person must verify payment state and approve sends.

evidence.reason: The native post names booking, assignment, payment-status and customer alerts plus retry and duplicate concerns, but gives no concrete field schema or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore merits a bounded proposed experiment, but no supplied implementation reference supports the mechanics; conservative provisional mean is below 6.

candidates.title: Inventory files before freeing disk space

demandEvidence.chore: Identify candidate files or categories for a person to review when freeing disk space.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Built a little native MacOS app out of necessity to help me free up some storage on my Mac.

experimentPlan.output: A read-only review list of large or duplicate-looking files from a supplied inventory.
inputs: synthetic file name and size rows
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator imports a fictional inventory table.
steps: Sort remaining rows by supplied size.
Group only rows with identical supplied hashes.
Show a review reason without changing files.
Compare the list with a manually checked expected result.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a synthetic inventory, verify protected rows never appear and sorting/grouping matches the answer key; confirm no file operation occurs.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies test inventory, checks every listed item and performs any device scan or deletion themselves.
unverified: Whether macOS exposes a safe inventory export
Whether hashes or duplicate detection are available
Any app, storage scanning or deletion capability

ease.reason: A student can test a manually supplied file inventory, but no reference supports Mac storage scanning or file metadata access.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: people with recurring storage pressure might pay for an inventory assistant; this personal account does not establish repeat demand or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can rank fictional inventory rows without touching files; safe real scanning and size accuracy are unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed report can sort supplied rows, but a person must verify every recommendation and perform any deletion; no autonomous device access is documented.

evidence.reason: The post states a personal need to free Mac storage and that an app was built, but supplies no frequency, workflow details or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore merits a bounded proposed experiment, but no supplied implementation reference supports the mechanics; conservative provisional mean is below 6.
